title: Uniqueness of the finite strict completed Koszul tensor augmentation
statement:
theorem completedKoszulTensorQuotientAugmentation_unique
    (r : ℕ) (a : Fin r → A)
    (β γ : completedKoszulTensorTower T d r a ⟶
      (completedAdicOrdinaryTower T d).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ))
    (hβ :
      (∀ (P : CochainComplex (CompletedAdicModules T d) ℤ) (n : ℕ),
        completedAdicKoszulTensorUnit T d r a P n ≫
          (HomologicalComplex.complexOfFunctorsToFunctorToComplex.map (β.app P)).app (op n) =
            completedQuotientTensorUnit T d P n) ∧
      (∀ (P : CochainComplex (CompletedAdicModules T d) ℤ) (n : ℕ) (p q : ℤ) (hq : q ≠ 0),
        completedKoszulTensorSummand T d r a P n p q ≫
            ((HomologicalComplex.complexOfFunctorsToFunctorToComplex.map
              (β.app P)).app (op n)).f (p + q) = 0))
    (hγ :
      (∀ (P : CochainComplex (CompletedAdicModules T d) ℤ) (n : ℕ),
        completedAdicKoszulTensorUnit T d r a P n ≫
          (HomologicalComplex.complexOfFunctorsToFunctorToComplex.map (γ.app P)).app (op n) =
            completedQuotientTensorUnit T d P n) ∧
      (∀ (P : CochainComplex (CompletedAdicModules T d) ℤ) (n : ℕ) (p q : ℤ) (hq : q ≠ 0),
        completedKoszulTensorSummand T d r a P n p q ≫
            ((HomologicalComplex.complexOfFunctorsToFunctorToComplex.map
              (γ.app P)).app (op n)).f (p + q) = 0)) :
    β = γ

proof.text: Prove that koszulConstantOne is invertible by constructing its inverse from the module sheafification Hom equivalence, sending the sheafification image of 1 to 1. The two inverse identities are tested on 1 using the unit-module Hom equivalence and the sheafification Hom equivalence. Composing its isomorphism with exteriorPower.zeroEquiv and the extension-by-zero degree-zero isomorphism makes koszulSheafUnitZero invertible.

Apply the scalar-extension unit isomorphism, whose inverse inserts 1, and then the normalized scalar-extension functor applied to koszulSheafUnitZero. Naturality of sheafification on pure tensors identifies the resulting map with completedAdicKoszulUnitZero by its specified value on 1. Thus this completed degree-zero unit is invertible. The scalar-extension coherence theorem is used only as a generic tool for its unit isomorphism and inverse section formula.

Apply natural-transformation extensionality at each input complex, complex degree, and tower index. Mathlib HomologicalComplex.mapBifunctor.hom_ext reduces equality of the component maps to equality after every total tensor summand inclusion. On the q=0 summand, take the degree-p component of the two unit normalization equations, and cancel the invertible right unitor and tensor of the degree-zero Koszul unit. For q nonzero, both composites vanish by the two vanishing hypotheses. These equalities prove equality of the original natural transformations.
